contexts.text: In His love and in His pity He redeemed them (). AE 412:7. TCR 116.
In the clemency of Jehovah upon him () = of grace and mercy.

The anger of Jehovah was kindled against Moses = clemency. The anger of Jehovah does not signify anger, but what is opposite to anger; thus mercy; here, clemency... because it is said in relation to Moses, by whom is represented the Lord as to Divine truth when He was in the world.
[Swedenborg footnote 1.] The Lord is pure mercy and clemency. References.
We contemplate the Divine omnipotence and clemency in these objects.
God, who is mercy and clemency itself... TCR 135:5.
A priest said... We believe that God the Father... excluded mankind from His clemency.
Propitiation means the operation of clemency and of grace...
Clemency cannot be injected into unmercifulness.
What would the Lord be, if he were to regard the evil from anger, and the good from clemency?
Thou hast had pity on the gourd... and should not I have pity on Nineveh (.)
